- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is still high, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5–7 day price action shows strong upward momentum, forecast should not exceed 1.5x recent high unless sentiment confirms strong bullish bias.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true price by 2–5% over 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to next forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, forecast should align with recent 10-day moving average, not 30-day trend.  
- Avoid forecasting spikes if sentiment is mixed or negative — model should lag 1–2 days behind true price if sentiment is uncertain.
